page: Microsoft Azure G3 is a G-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this server features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 112.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 14.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance is equipped with 1573 GB of local storage, while containing no GPU accelerators. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates distinct performance profiles and tradeoffs. The single-core and multi-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the poor and weak categories respectively, reflecting the older 2.0 GHz processor architecture. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for small-block cached reads, but drop to weak and poor categories for large-block uncached reads and writes. Despite these limitations, the server achieves average scores in Passmark CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core workloads, and Redis SET operations, demonstrating stable performance for standard transactional tasks.

Given the high memory capacity of 112.0 GB and substantial 1573 GB local storage, the G3 instance is qualitatively positioned as a memory-and-storage-heavy resource. While its raw compute and memory write speeds are limited, the large memory footprint and local storage capacity make it suitable for database operations, memory-intensive legacy applications, and moderate web serving. It is less suitable for compute-heavy tasks or large-scale language model inference, where benchmarks show poor performance.
